rendered: The authors did not train a random forest, a neural network, or any similar machine-learning classifier. Neither term appears anywhere in the document.[1] Instead, they classified the bacteria with a standard statistical method: linear discriminant analysis (LDA)[2]. They ran it in Origin 2026 and SPSS v27.0 software[3]. The paper calls it the statistical method of linear[4] discriminant analysis. The LDA score plots were built from the two principal discriminant factors[5]. In those plots, the clusters for the different bacterial species do not overlap (Fig. 2[6]). The authors also used hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA[7] to check how the samples group. HCA is an unsupervised clustering method, not a trained classifier.
